chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Al-Hakam ibn Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Amr ibn Harith al-Ashja'i, from Bardha'a ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Khalil, from Salman (may God's mercy be upon him). He said: I visited the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) when he was dying,
and he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib is the best of those I leave behind me.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Most excellent, best — a superlative of virtue and rank, used to assert Ali's supremacy among all remaining companions
key_terms.بَعْدِي: After me — indicating the Prophet's acknowledgment of his own imminent departure and concern for the community's leadership
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ: At the time of death — the deathbed context lends special gravity and finality to the Prophet's words

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Ali ibn Abi Talib on his deathbed according to Salman al-Farisi?
ai.summary: Salman al-Farisi narrates that he visited the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) at the moment of his death, and the Prophet declared Ali ibn Abi Talib to be the best person he was leaving behind. This narration is among the deathbed testimonies of the Prophet asserting the superiority of Imam Ali, which Shia tradition views as confirming his rightful succession. The hadith is transmitted through the Amali of Shaykh Saduq via a chain tracing back to Salman, one of the most trusted companions.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Al-Hakam b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Hashim narrated to us from `Amr b. Harith al-Ashja`i from Bardha`a b. `Abd al-Rahman from Abi'l Khalil from Salman (rh). He said: I visited the Messenger of Allah (s) when he was dying,
and he said: `Ali b. Abi Talib is the best [person] I leave behind.
